item.title: COMPOL Tudravu to recruits: Toe the line or leave
item.description: Police Commissioner Rusiate Tudravu has issued a firm warning to 185 new police recruits that those unable to meet the Fiji Police Force’s standards of discipline will not make it through their six-month training. Opening the Batch 70 Basic Recruit Course at the Fiji Police Academy yesterday, Mr Tudravu stressed that discipline would be non-negotiable throughout the training.
item.content:encoded:
Police Commissioner Rusiate Tudravu has issued a firm warning to 185 new police recruits that those unable to meet the Fiji Police Force’s standards of discipline will not make it through their six-month training.

Opening the Batch 70 Basic Recruit Course at the Fiji Police Academy yesterday, Mr Tudravu stressed that discipline would be non-negotiable throughout the training.

“If you cannot toe the line, the gates remain open, and you have seen that I have been serious about this from the moment you marched in,” Mr Tudravu told the recruits.

“Let’s get rid of the bad apples and ensure only the cream of the crop will march out at the end of the six months.”

The Commissioner said he expected the best from the recruits and wanted future officers who were physically and mentally capable of dealing with the challenges they would encounter on the frontline.

He reminded them that policing was not simply about acquiring technical knowledge and skills, but also about developing character, leadership and the right attitude towards the communities they would serve.

“Your training here is not just about acquiring policing knowledge and skills, but also about developing the character, leadership qualities, and community-focused mindset required to serve the people of Fiji and Tuvalu effectively,” he said.

Mr Tudravu also welcomed 14 recruits from Tuvalu and encouraged them to regard the Fiji Police Academy as their home during the training period.

He told the recruits their conduct would be expected to reflect the standards of the organisation both on and off duty.

“This means your every action, your every being, from the way you talk to people, on or off duty, the way you treat your work, must always be aligned to the organizational mission and vision,” Mr Tudravu said.

“Anything less is a disservice to your oath, the police uniform and organization.”

The six-month training for Batch 70 is scheduled to conclude on February 12, 2027.

item.title: Auditor-General flags governance failures across municipal councils
item.description: The Auditor-General has raised serious concerns over financial reporting, governance and internal controls across Fiji’s municipal councils after modified audit opinions were issued on all 19 financial statements audited. In its Report on Municipal Councils, the Auditor-General said the findings reflected negatively on the councils and required urgent attention from those responsible for their gov
item.content:encoded:
The Auditor-General has raised serious concerns over financial reporting, governance and internal controls across Fiji’s municipal councils after modified audit opinions were issued on all 19 financial statements audited.

In its Report on Municipal Councils, the Auditor-General said the findings reflected negatively on the councils and required urgent attention from those responsible for their governance.

This report includes the audit results of 19 financial statements for 8 Municipal Councils as follows:

-Nausori Town Council 2019 to 2021 -Tavua Town Council 2021 to 2023 -Rakiraki Town Council 2024 & 2025 -Levuka Town Council 2019 -Savusavu Town Council 2018 to 2020 -Suva City Council 2020 -Labasa Town Council 2019 to 2021 -Lami Town Council 2021 to 2023

“Urgent attention should be given to address matters which have been highlighted in the Auditors’ Reports,” the report stated.

A major concern identified was the quality and timeliness of financial reporting, with delays in submitting financial statements preventing the Auditor-General from providing Parliament and other stakeholders with timely audit findings.

“Improving the quality and timeliness of financial reporting is a major concern that needs to be addressed by those charged with governance of the Municipal Councils,” the report said.

The audit also found weaknesses in governance and internal controls, with some regulations, formal policies and procedures either outdated or non-existent.

“Good governance and internal controls are lacking because regulations, formal policies and procedures to govern all aspects of the Municipal Councils’ operations were not reviewed and updated for a long period of time or that they do not exist,” the report stated.

Poor records management was another concern, with the Auditor-General noting missing financial records and the absence of a policy specifically addressing effective records management.

The report recommended that improving financial statements be treated as an “utmost priority”, including employing suitably qualified accountants capable of preparing financial statements on time.

It also recommended establishing a robust audit, risk and improvement committee to address financial reporting, governance and internal control deficiencies.

Municipal councils were further urged to maintain accurate fixed-asset records and develop clear plans for asset valuations.

“The Ministry of Local Government should continue to strengthen its monitoring role on the operations of the Municipal Councils to improve financial accountability,” the Auditor-General said.

item.title: FHTA welcomes Government shift on tourism tax
item.description: The Fiji Hotel and Tourism Association has welcomed Government’s decision to exempt existing bookings from the new Tourism Services Tax, describing the change as the outcome the industry had sought since consultations began. Government has confirmed that the five per cent TST will apply only to bookings made on or after September 1, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Hotel and Tourism Association has welcomed Government’s decision to exempt existing bookings from the new Tourism Services Tax, describing the change as the outcome the industry had sought since consultations began.

Government has confirmed that the five per cent TST will apply only to bookings made on or after September 1, 2026.

This means bookings made before that date will not attract the tax, even if the tourism service is provided after September 1.

FHTA chief executive officer Fantasha Lockington said the decision removed uncertainty for visitors who had booked and paid for their Fiji holidays months before the tax was due to take effect.

“This is a genuinely welcome result, and the right one,” Ms Lockington said.

“It restores fairness for visitors who planned their holiday in good faith, and it removes a real source of confusion and the higher risk of booking cancellations for the industry.”

She also acknowledged Government’s stated commitment to listening to the tourism industry and working collaboratively on policies supporting sustainable economic growth.

FHTA had consistently pushed for existing bookings to be exempt, arguing that visitors should not face an additional tax that did not exist when they booked their holidays.

Despite welcoming the change, the association said further clarity was still needed before implementation.

FHTA is awaiting updated Standard Interpretation Guidelines and further guidance from the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service on the scope and application of the tax.

“While not complete in terms of the clarity around the application, we are absolutely delighted with the outcome,” Ms Lockington said.

“Members still need clear, practical answers before 1 September.”

She said FHTA would continue working with FRCS despite the increasingly limited time available for tourism businesses to update their systems.

The five per cent TST will apply for 12 months from September 1, 2026, to specified tourism businesses with annual turnover of $2 million or more and to specified tourism services.

item.title: Fiji Airways to stop direct Canberra-Nadi flights, Canberra Times reports
item.description: Fiji Airways will suspend its direct flights between Canberra and Nadi early next year, citing challenging market conditions. According to a report by The Canberra Times , Fiji Airways informed affected passengers that the service would be suspended from February 5, 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Airways will suspend its direct flights between Canberra and Nadi early next year, citing challenging market conditions.

According to a report by The Canberra Times , Fiji Airways informed affected passengers that the service would be suspended from February 5, 2027.

“Due to market conditions, we have taken the difficult decision to suspend our Canberra to Nadi services effective 5th February 2027,” the airline reportedly told a passenger booked to travel after that date.

Fiji Airways told The Canberra Times that travellers from Canberra would still be able to reach Fiji through its daily Sydney-Nadi services, which it said were already used by many Canberra passengers.

The airline described the decision as a suspension but did not provide a date for the route’s possible resumption.

The Canberra-Nadi route was launched three years ago with considerable fanfare and initially operated three times a week.

Canberra Airport Head of Aviation Michael Thomson said global uncertainty, rising aviation fuel prices and weaker demand for travel to the United States had affected the viability of the service.

“The impacts of global uncertainty, continued escalation of fuel prices and softer demand for travel to the United States have currently made the service challenging to sustain,” Mr Thomson told The Canberra Times .

He described Fiji Airways’ decision as disappointing but expressed hope the airline would eventually return.

“We thank Fiji Airways for its commitment to Canberra and look forward to welcoming them back when the economic conditions improve,” he said.

Mr Thomson said Canberra Airport remained focused on expanding direct international connectivity for the region.

Fiji Airways’ withdrawal will bring an end, at least temporarily, to Canberra’s direct air connection with Nadi, requiring Fiji-bound passengers to consider connecting services, including through Sydney.

item.title: NFP demands action on crime
item.description: National Federation Party president Parmod Chand has called on Police Commissioner Rusiate Tudravu to increase police visibility amid concerns over robberies, burglaries and attacks on taxi drivers. Mr Chand said law-abiding people should not feel unsafe in their homes and communities while criminal activity continued in public spaces and residential areas.
item.content:encoded:
National Federation Party president Parmod Chand has called on Police Commissioner Rusiate Tudravu to increase police visibility amid concerns over robberies, burglaries and attacks on taxi drivers.

Mr Chand said law-abiding people should not feel unsafe in their homes and communities while criminal activity continued in public spaces and residential areas.

“Public spaces belong to families, workers, students and businesses, not to people using them to threaten others or plan criminal activity,” he said.

He highlighted recent alleged attacks on taxi drivers in Wainibokasi and Nadi, as well as reports of robberies, purse snatching and an attempted stabbing in Cunningham.

Mr Chand said several incidents had occurred in broad daylight, with some receiving greater attention only after CCTV footage circulated publicly.

“The Commissioner must treat the fear being expressed by communities as a serious operational warning,” he said.

Mr Chand pointed to significant funding allocated to the Fiji Police Force in recent national budgets, including funding for additional officers and police beat patrols.

He said the public was entitled to know where additional officers had been deployed and whether the investment had resulted in increased police presence.

The NFP is calling for intensified foot and mobile patrols around residential areas, taxi bases, bus stands, markets and identified crime hotspots, as well as stronger night patrols and targeted operations.

Mr Chand also called for Crime Prevention Committees to be reactivated and for divisional crime and detection statistics to be made public.

“Effective policing cannot depend on waiting for a crime to be recorded on CCTV and circulated on social media,” he said.

“Police must be visible before an offence occurs, not only after the victim has been assaulted or robbed.”

Mr Chand said Government had provided funding, additional personnel and reforms, and these resources now needed to translate into “visible patrols, safer public spaces and decisive action.”

item.title: Police hunt fourth suspect in Nadi taxi robbery case
item.description: The Fiji Police Force is searching for a person of interest wanted in connection with the alleged aggravated robbery of a taxi driver in Nadi yesterday. Police have released an image of the person and are calling on him to surrender at the nearest police station.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Police Force is searching for a person of interest wanted in connection with the alleged aggravated robbery of a taxi driver in Nadi yesterday.

Police have released an image of the person and are calling on him to surrender at the nearest police station.

The alleged robbery involving the taxi driver was captured on a dash camera, with footage of the incident subsequently going viral on social media.

Three suspects are already in Police custody in connection with the incident.

“The Fiji Police Force is calling on the individual to present and surrender himself at a nearby Police Station,” Police said.

The Western Division Taskforce has been pursuing those allegedly involved since the incident was reported.

Members of the public who have information about the whereabouts of the person of interest have been urged to contact Police.

Information can be provided through 1681, Nadi Police Station on 2296 506, or the Western Division Police Command Centre on 9905 457.

Investigations into the alleged aggravated robbery continue.

item.title: Tuisawau condemns attack on Nadi taxi driver
item.description: Minister for Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport Ro Filipe Tuisawau has strongly condemned the recent attack on a taxi driver in Nadi, saying public service vehicle drivers should not have to risk their lives while earning a living. Mr Tuisawau said taxi drivers and other PSV operators provided an essential service, transporting thousands of Fijians daily to workplaces, schools, bu
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport Ro Filipe Tuisawau has strongly condemned the recent attack on a taxi driver in Nadi, saying public service vehicle drivers should not have to risk their lives while earning a living.

Mr Tuisawau said taxi drivers and other PSV operators provided an essential service, transporting thousands of Fijians daily to workplaces, schools, businesses and health facilities.

“PSV drivers are working hard to earn a living while providing an essential service to the public,” he said.

“They should be able to do their jobs without fear that a routine passenger interaction or disagreement could place their safety, their lives or their livelihoods at risk.”

His comments follow an alleged aggravated robbery involving a taxi driver in Nadi that was captured on the vehicle’s dash camera and subsequently went viral on social media.

While stressing that Police investigations should be allowed to continue, Mr Tuisawau urged people to refrain from violence, intimidation and other criminal behaviour against public transport operators.

“Our PSV drivers are members of our communities. They are parents, family members and individuals working hard to provide for their families,” he said.

“There is absolutely no justification for violence or criminal behaviour against them.”

Mr Tuisawau also reminded PSV drivers that they were required to provide services in accordance with their permit conditions and should not unlawfully refuse passengers.

However, he said those obligations should not prevent drivers from protecting themselves when they genuinely feared for their safety.

“No driver should feel compelled to remain in a situation where they reasonably fear for their life or safety,” he said.

He urged drivers confronted with threatening situations to prioritise their safety, leave the situation where possible and seek immediate Police assistance or proceed to the nearest police station.

Mr Tuisawau said PSV operators should never have to choose between protecting their livelihoods and their personal safety.

He also called on passengers to treat drivers with respect and resolve disagreements peacefully.

“Public transport is a shared responsibility. We all have a role to play in ensuring our PSV drivers can carry out their work safely and return home to their families at the end of the day,” Mr Tuisawau said.

He said Government remained committed to maintaining a safe, reliable and accessible public transport system while protecting the rights and safety of those providing the services.

item.title: Central has biggest voter share – Mataiciwa
item.description: THE Central Division has the largest share of Fiji’s registered voters, accounting for more than 43 per cent of the country’s total voter register. This, according to a statement by the Fiji Elections Office which shows a national total of 723,771 registered voters as of June this year.
item.content:encoded:
THE Central Division has the largest share of Fiji’s registered voters, accounting for more than 43 per cent of the country’s total voter register.

This, according to a statement by the Fiji Elections Office which shows a national total of 723,771 registered voters as of June this year.

Supervisor of Elections, Ana Mataiciwa, said the updated figures provide the FEO with an important basis for its preparations for the upcoming General Election.

From the total registered voters, 362,438 are male, and 361,333 are female.

Ms Mataiciwa said the updated figures will guide the FEO’s preparations for the upcoming General Election, including its planning for polling operations and voter services.

The figures show a significant concentration of registered voters in Fiji’s two largest divisions, with the Central and Western divisions together accounting for more than four out of every five voters on the register.

The Central Division has 313,135 registered voters, representing approximately 43.3 per cent of the national total.

The Western Division follows with 270,175 voters, or approximately 37.3 per cent.

Combined, the two divisions have 583,310 registered voters, accounting for approximately 80.6 per cent of all registered voters.

The Northern Division has 102,304 registered voters, making up approximately 14.1 per cent of the national register.

This leaves less than 6 per cent of registered voters spread across the Eastern Division and overseas.

The Eastern Division has 25,266 voters, equivalent to approximately 3.5 per cent of the national total, while the 12,891 overseas voters make up the remaining 1.8 per cent of all registered voters.
